decisions.executionNote: Begin left-arm elbow-up approach toward the central coin; bank is in right workspace. Keep right arm parked.
Replan after continuity guard with smaller orientation changes, bringing the left wrist inward and up.
Advance left arm toward coin while progressively pitching the open gripper downward; retain continuous elbow-up motion.
Continue the open left gripper approach above the central holder, with gradual downward orientation.
Move the left wrist closer to the holder with the coin now visible at the edge of the wrist view; continue slow downward pitching.
Approach from above while centering the coin in the left wrist view; keep the gripper open and right arm clear.
Finish aligning the downward left gripper above the coin, using small translation and rotation increments before grasping.
Fine-center the coin between the open jaws and align their closing direction with the coin faces; lower cautiously.
Correct lateral and yaw alignment from the wrist image; maintain height while centering the coin before closing.
Make the final millimeter-scale centering and yaw adjustment, then begin closing the left jaws around the coin.
Correct the remaining small wrist-image offset and close fully on the coin, holding position to establish the grasp.
The coin remains off-center in the wrist image. Reopen slightly and correct lateral alignment before attempting retention.
Coin is nearly centered between the jaws. Close fully and make a short vertical test lift, checking RGB for retention.
Raise the closed left gripper vertically to clear the holder and verify the coin remains between the jaws.
The coin appears to have slipped out toward the right. Clear the left arm and begin a cautious right-arm recovery approach while checking the settled coin.
Clear the left workspace and pitch the right gripper down toward the fallen coin; its position is still settling.
Continue right-arm approach to the settled coin and move the left wrist farther away, maintaining elbow-up continuity.
Bring the right wrist above the coin with a gradual downward rotation, while leaving the left arm safely in its own workspace.
Center the open right jaws over the fallen coin and finish the downward approach; assess the coin's flat orientation before grasping.
Finish positioning the downward right gripper over the flat coin, then inspect alignment before lowering to the rim.
Lower the centered right gripper toward the flat coin rim while narrowing the jaws, with small vertical increments.
Close the right jaws on opposite sides of the coin rim, pause, and begin a minimal test lift.
Lift vertically with the right gripper closed and check whether the coin stays attached rather than sliding on the table.
The coin did not follow the lift. Reopen and approach its rim again with a small forward correction and lower grasp height.
Set the right fingertips slightly lower around the rim, fine-center laterally, and close fully without lifting yet.
Hold the right jaws closed, then make a slow short lift to test whether the coin is retained.
Continue the slow closed-gripper test lift and inspect coin retention against the background.
The coin remains on the tabletop. Reopen and lower the fingertips for a deeper rim grasp rather than repeating the shallow pinch.
Use a lower rim-level pinch with two-millimeter descent steps, then close fully and inspect before lifting.
Relieve tabletop contact slightly, square the right fingertips to the coin plane, and attempt a level rim pinch.
Re-center over the visible coin and remove the small remaining wrist tilt, keeping the fingertips just above the tabletop.
Reopen to avoid pushing the coin, correct the lateral offset in the wrist view, and return gently to rim height.
Coin is now centered at the jaw tips. Make a level rim pinch, settle closed, and test with a three-millimeter lift.
Lift the closed right gripper slowly, checking that the coin rim remains supported between both fingertips.
Coin now visibly follows the right fingertips. Raise it clear of the tabletop with the jaws kept closed.
Lift and translate the retained coin toward the bank while gradually rotating it upright, keeping the coin well clear of the bank.
Continue carrying the coin above the bank with a gradual upright rotation and keep the closed grasp unchanged.
Move toward the bank-side approach pose while continuing to rotate the coin into a vertical plane; monitor secure retention.
Gradually align the upright coin plane with the bank slot direction, approaching from the front with clearance.
Continue the gradual upright alignment above the bank, lowering only while the coin remains clear of the slot surface.
Replan from the interrupted pose using smaller increments; align the upright coin with the visible slot while retaining overhead clearance.
Continue small, continuous adjustments to bring the vertical coin directly above the slot without releasing it.
Use the head view to correct the coin leftward toward the slot and finish its vertical orientation, lowering conservatively.
Back slightly away from the wrist rotation limit after the rejection, using millimeter-scale slot approach corrections and maintaining the closed grasp.
The approach is constrained near the bank. Lift clear and begin rolling the wrist around the held coin's axis to obtain an unobstructed insertion posture.
Continue rolling the retained coin in free space toward a clear insertion posture, while gradually returning the empty left arm toward home.
Roll the held coin about its normal with safe clearance, avoiding the wrist limit; continue the empty left arm's gradual return.
Continue the unobstructed wrist roll without translating the retained coin; bring the empty left arm closer to home.
Continue rotating the grasp in free space toward a wrist-neutral insertion configuration while retracting the empty left arm.
Finish most of the free-space wrist roll, keeping the coin securely pinched and the arms in separate workspaces.
Square the now-clear right wrist to the slot direction and begin lowering the retained upright coin above the bank.
Lower the upright retained coin toward the slot in six-millimeter increments, while completing the empty left arm's return.
Bring the coin closer to the slot vertically, keeping its plane aligned and the grasp closed; finish retracting the empty left arm.
Use small vertical insertion increments while keeping the coin upright and closed in the right gripper; return the left wrist to its initial pose.
Relieve contact near the bank by pivoting the wrist upward around the retained coin, obtaining a clearer view of the slot before precise release.
After the continuity rejection, use half-sized pivot increments to free the gripper body while preserving the coin's position above the bank.
Shift the coin laterally over the slot and restore its vertical plane with a small pivot, preserving its height for a controlled release.
Fine-position the upright coin over the calibrated slot location while holding height and keeping the grasp closed.

Keep the jaws open while the released coin settles, then begin a small upward withdrawal without contacting the bank.
